question:
An 8-year old boy is brought to the emergency department because he has been lethargic and has had several episodes of nausea and vomiting for the past day. He has also had increased thirst over the past two months. He has lost 5.4 kg (11.9 lbs) during this time. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of serious illness. His temperature is 37.5 °C (99.5 °F), blood pressure is 95/68 mm Hg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 30/min. He is somnolent and slightly confused. His mucous membranes are dry. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 16.2 g/dL
Leukocyte count 9,500/mm3
Platelet count 380,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 130 mEq/L
K+ 5.5 mEq/L
Cl- 99 mEq/L
HCO3- 16 mEq/L
Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL
Glucose 570 mg/dL
Ketones positive
Blood gases, arterial
pH 7.25
pCO2 21 mm Hg
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?"?

options.opa: Intravenous hydration with 0.9% normal saline and insulin
options.opb: Intravenous hydration with 5% dextrose solution and 0.45% normal saline
options.opc: Intravenous hydration with 0.45% normal saline and insulin
options.opd: Intravenous hydration with 0.9% normal saline and potassium chloride

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: High glucose levels -> hyperglycemia -> osmotic diuresis -> dehydration -> lethargy, nausea, vomiting, increased thirst, weight loss -> metabolic acidosis -> confusion, somnolence -> 80%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) characterized by hyperglycemia, ketosis, metabolic acidosis, and dehydration. The most appropriate next step in management would be to initiate intravenous hydration with 0.9% normal saline and insulin to correct the dehydration and hyperglycemia.
